mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is positive for corporate earnings and thus drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when UNRATE is below 4% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic expansion, leading to higher S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and profits grow.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: Forward returns are negative when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive returns when HOUST increases by 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) alongside low unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate inflationary pressures, negatively impacting equity valuations.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur under the specified conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates robust economic activity, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth (PAYEMS) paired with controlled inflation (CPIAUCSL) supports economic stability, driving positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns under the specified conditions.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, lower federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) stimulate borrowing, boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: No positive returns when FEDFUNDS are low in late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer spending, driving corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns when RSAFS grows over 0.5% MoM.
